findings.reason: the node would land a shared builder and re-point a negative control at a point where the mutation cannot bite, so the plan loses the only coverage that shows the figure revision reaches the row, and the fixture must instead be re-pointed at the index's own row assembly (or at `file_revision`).
findings.text: §16's done-when says the negative-control fixture in `tests/test_a_figure_revision_is_fetched_once.py` "is rewritten to patch the builder the index now calls, and the file's cases are otherwise unchanged and pass", but under the deliverable the index adds `revision` itself after the builder returns (only `created`, `edited` and `revision` are what the index "alone carries"), so a wrapper around the builder that pops `revision` removes nothing, the mutation becomes indistinguishable from the unarmed arm, and the test's declared control stops firing while its cases still pass — the same shape as a guard that reports protection it does not provide

findings.reason: the node would implement the projection literally, or leave the conversion unnamed, and a page painting from the index would lose the figure dimensions §3 declares its rows carry, with the new test green over the loss; the plan should name the dimension conversion (or have the builder emit `width`/`height`) and assert the index row keeps them.
findings.text: §16's deliverable has the index call the shared builder and add "only what it alone carries (its `created` and `edited` stamps and its `revision`), projected onto `ROW_FIELDS`", but the two rows name dimensions differently — the builder that `figure_rows` builds today carries `dims`, a formatted string (`reckon/figures.py:54-55`, `:192`), while the index row carries `width` and `height` as integers and `ROW_FIELDS` names `width` and `height` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:62-76`, `:1246-1247`), and the plan's Why describes the two copies as deriving "the same fields" including dimensions — so the projection as written drops `width`/`height` unless a conversion rule the plan never states is added, and the done-when cannot catch it because its agreement case compares only the four fields the two rows share by name (`slug`, `type`, `title`, `href`)
